units.leftText: A revelation about Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.
units.rightText: This is the burden against Nineveh, the book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite:

units.leftText: The LORD is a jealous God and avenges. The LORD avenges and is full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on his adversaries, and he maintains wrath against his enemies.
units.rightText: The LORD is a jealous and avenging God; the LORD is avenging and full of wrath. The LORD takes vengeance on His foes and reserves wrath for His enemies.
leftNotes: 1:2 When rendered in ALL CAPITAL LETTERS, “LORD” or “GOD” is the translation of God’s Proper Name (Hebrew “יהוה*”, usually pronounced Yahweh).

units.leftText: The LORD is slow to anger, and great in power, and will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. The LORD has his way in the whirlwind and in the storm, and the clouds are the dust of his feet.
units.rightText: The LORD is slow to anger and great in power; the LORD will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. His path is in the whirlwind and storm, and clouds are the dust beneath His feet.

units.leftText: He rebukes the sea and makes it dry, and dries up all the rivers. Bashan and Carmel languish. The flower of Lebanon languishes.
units.rightText: He rebukes the sea and dries it up; He makes all the rivers run dry. Bashan and Carmel wither, and the flower of Lebanon wilts.

units.leftText: The mountains quake before him, and the hills melt away. The earth trembles at his presence, yes, the world, and all who dwell in it.
units.rightText: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence— the world and all its dwellers.

units.leftText: Who can stand before his indignation? Who can endure the fierceness of his anger? His wrath is poured out like fire, and the rocks are broken apart by him.
units.rightText: Who can withstand His indignation? Who can endure His burning anger? His wrath is poured out like fire; even rocks are shattered before Him.

units.leftText: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble; and he knows those who take refuge in him.
units.rightText: The LORD is good, a stronghold in the day of distress; He cares for those who trust in Him.

units.leftText: But with an overflowing flood, he will make a full end of her place, and will pursue his enemies into darkness.
units.rightText: But with an overwhelming flood He will make an end of Nineveh and pursue His enemies into darkness.

units.leftText: What do you plot against the LORD? He will make a full end. Affliction won’t rise up the second time.
units.rightText: Whatever you plot against the LORD, He will bring to an end. Affliction will not rise up a second time.

units.leftText: For entangled like thorns, and drunken as with their drink, they are consumed utterly like dry stubble.
units.rightText: For they will be entangled as with thorns and consumed like the drink of a drunkard — like stubble that is fully dry.

units.leftText: One has gone out of you who devises evil against the LORD, who counsels wickedness.
units.rightText: From you, O Nineveh, comes forth a plotter of evil against the LORD, a counselor of wickedness.

units.leftText: The LORD says: “Though they are in full strength and likewise many, even so they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, I will afflict you no more.
units.rightText: This is what the LORD says: “Though they are allied and numerous, yet they will be cut down and pass away. Though I have afflicted you, O Judah, I will afflict you no longer.

units.leftText: Now I will break his yoke from off you, and will burst your bonds apart.”
units.rightText: For I will now break their yoke from your neck and tear away your shackles.”

units.leftText: The LORD has commanded concerning you: “No more descendants will bear your name. Out of the house of your gods, I will cut off the engraved image and the molten image. I will make your grave, for you are vile.”
units.rightText: The LORD has issued a command concerning you, O Nineveh: “There will be no descendants to carry on your name. I will cut off the carved image and cast idol from the house of your gods; I will prepare your grave, for you are contemptible.”

units.leftText: Behold, on the mountains the feet of him who brings good news, who publishes peace! Keep your feasts, Judah! Perform your vows, for the wicked one will no more pass through you. He is utterly cut off.
units.rightText: Look to the mountains— the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the wicked will never again march through you; they will be utterly cut off.
leftNotes: 1:15 “Behold”, from “הִנֵּה*”, means look at, take notice, observe, see, or gaze at. It is often used as an interjection.

units.leftText: He who dashes in pieces has come up against you. Keep the fortress! Watch the way! Strengthen your waist! Fortify your power mightily!
units.rightText: One who scatters advances against you, O Nineveh. Guard the fortress! Watch the road! Brace yourselves! Summon all your strength!

units.leftText: For the LORD restores the excellency of Jacob as the excellency of Israel, for the destroyers have destroyed them and ruined their vine branches.
units.rightText: For the LORD will restore the splendor of Jacob like the splendor of Israel, though destroyers have laid them waste and ruined the branches of their vine.

units.leftText: The shield of his mighty men is made red. The valiant men are in scarlet. The chariots flash with steel in the day of his preparation, and the pine spears are brandished.
units.rightText: The shields of his mighty men are red; the valiant warriors are dressed in scarlet. The fittings of the chariots flash like fire on the day they are prepared, and the spears of cypress have been brandished.
rightNotes: 2:3 Hebrew; alternately, the spears may be of pine or juniper or fir; LXX and Syriac they are prepared, and the horsemen rush to and fro.

units.leftText: The chariots rage in the streets. They rush back and forth in the wide ways. Their appearance is like torches. They run like the lightnings.
units.rightText: The chariots dash through the streets; they rush around the plazas, appearing like torches, darting about like lightning.

units.leftText: He summons his picked troops. They stumble on their way. They dash to its wall, and the protective shield is put in place.
units.rightText: He summons his nobles; they stumble as they advance. They race to its wall; the protective shield is set in place.

units.leftText: The gates of the rivers are opened, and the palace is dissolved.
units.rightText: The river gates are thrown open and the palace collapses.

units.leftText: It is decreed: she is uncovered, she is carried away; and her servants moan as with the voice of doves, beating on their breasts.
units.rightText: It is decreed that the city be exiled and carried away; her maidservants moan like doves, and beat upon their breasts.

units.leftText: But Nineveh has been from of old like a pool of water, yet they flee away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one looks back.
units.rightText: Nineveh has been like a pool of water throughout her days, but now it is draining away. “Stop! Stop!” they cry, but no one turns back.

units.leftText: Take the plunder of silver. Take the plunder of gold, for there is no end of treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.
units.rightText: “Plunder the silver! Plunder the gold!” There is no end to the treasure, an abundance of every precious thing.

units.leftText: She is empty, void, and waste. The heart melts, the knees knock together, their bodies and faces have grown pale.
units.rightText: She is emptied! Yes , she is desolate and laid waste! Hearts melt, knees knock, bodies tremble, and every face grows pale!

units.leftText: Where is the den of the lions, and the feeding place of the young lions, where the lion and the lioness walked with the lion’s cubs, and no one made them afraid?
units.rightText: Where is the lions’ lair or the feeding ground of the young lions, where the lion and lioness prowled with their cubs, with nothing to frighten them away?

units.leftText: The lion tore in pieces enough for his cubs, and strangled prey for his lionesses, and filled his caves with the kill and his dens with prey.
units.rightText: The lion mauled enough for its cubs and strangled prey for the lioness. It filled its dens with the kill, and its lairs with mauled prey.

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will burn her chariots in the smoke, and the sword will devour your young lions; and I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voice of your messengers will no longer be heard.”
units.rightText: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will reduce your chariots to cinders, and the sword will devour your young lions. I will cut off your prey from the earth, and the voices of your messengers will no longer be heard.”

units.leftText: Woe to the bloody city! It is all full of lies and robbery—no end to the prey.
units.rightText: Woe to the city of blood, full of lies, full of plunder, never without prey.

units.leftText: The noise of the whip, the noise of the rattling of wheels, prancing horses, and bounding chariots,
units.rightText: The crack of the whip, the rumble of the wheel, galloping horse and bounding chariot!

units.leftText: the horseman charging, and the flashing sword, the glittering spear, and a multitude of slain, and a great heap of corpses, and there is no end of the bodies. They stumble on their bodies
units.rightText: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end— they stumble over their dead—

units.leftText: because of the multitude of the prostitution of the alluring prostitute, the mistress of witchcraft, who sells nations through her prostitution, and families through her witchcraft.
units.rightText: because of the many harlotries of the harlot, the seductive mistress of sorcery, who betrays nations by her prostitution and clans by her witchcraft.

units.leftText: “Behold, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies, “and I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show the nations your nakedness, and the kingdoms your shame.
units.rightText: “Behold, I am against you,” declares the LORD of Hosts. “I will lift your skirts over your face. I will show your nakedness to the nations and your shame to the kingdoms.

units.leftText: I will throw abominable filth on you and make you vile, and will make you a spectacle.
units.rightText: I will pelt you with filth and treat you with contempt; I will make a spectacle of you.

units.leftText: It will happen that all those who look at you will flee from you, and say, ‘Nineveh is laid waste! Who will mourn for her?’ Where will I seek comforters for you?”
units.rightText: Then all who see you will recoil from you and say, ‘Nineveh is devastated; who will grieve for her?’ Where can I find comforters for you?”

units.leftText: Are you better than No-Amon, who was situated among the rivers, who had the waters around her, whose rampart was the sea, and her wall was of the sea?
units.rightText: Are you better than Thebes, stationed by the Nile with water around her, whose rampart was the sea, whose wall was the water?

units.leftText: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength. Put and Libya were her helpers.
units.rightText: Cush and Egypt were her boundless strength; Put and Libya were her allies.
rightNotes: 3:9 That is, the upper Nile region

units.leftText: Yet was she carried away. She went into captivity. Her young children also were dashed in pieces at the head of all the streets, and they cast lots for her honorable men, and all her great men were bound in chains.
units.rightText: Yet she became an exile; she went into captivity. Her infants were dashed to pieces at the head of every street. They cast lots for her dignitaries, and all her nobles were bound in chains.

units.leftText: You also will be drunken. You will be hidden. You also will seek a stronghold because of the enemy.
units.rightText: You too will become drunk; you will go into hiding and seek refuge from the enemy.

units.leftText: All your fortresses will be like fig trees with the first-ripe figs. If they are shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater.
units.rightText: All your fortresses are fig trees with the first ripe figs; when shaken, they fall into the mouth of the eater!

units.leftText: Behold, your troops among you are women. The gates of your land are set wide open to your enemies. The fire has devoured your bars.
units.rightText: Look at your troops — they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.

units.leftText: Draw water for the siege. Strengthen your fortresses. Go into the clay, and tread the mortar. Make the brick kiln strong.
units.rightText: Draw your water for the siege; strengthen your fortresses. Work the clay and tread the mortar; repair the brick kiln!

units.leftText: There the fire will devour you. The sword will cut you off. It will devour you like the grasshopper. Multiply like grasshoppers. Multiply like the locust.
units.rightText: There the fire will devour you; the sword will cut you down and consume you like a young locust. Make yourself many like the young locust; make yourself many like the swarming locust!

units.leftText: You have increased your merchants more than the stars of the skies. The grasshopper strips and flees away.
units.rightText: You have multiplied your merchants more than the stars of the sky. The young locust strips the land and flies away.

units.leftText: Your guards are like the locusts, and your officials like the swarms of locusts, which settle on the walls on a cold day, but when the sun appears, they flee away, and their place is not known where they are.
units.rightText: Your guards are like the swarming locust, and your scribes like clouds of locusts that settle on the walls on a cold day. When the sun rises, they fly away, and no one knows where.

units.leftText: Your shepherds slumber, king of Assyria. Your nobles lie down. Your people are scattered on the mountains, and there is no one to gather them.
units.rightText: O king of Assyria, your shepherds slumber; your officers sleep. Your people are scattered on the mountains with no one to gather them.

units.leftText: There is no healing your wound, for your injury is fatal. All who hear the report of you clap their hands over you, for who hasn’t felt your endless cruelty?
units.rightText: There is no healing for your injury; your wound is severe. All who hear the news of you applaud your downfall, for who has not experienced your constant cruelty?
